drafted_from: tools/meaning-search/tool-rows.json (tool:make-a-picture-vector-set-of-my-videos), do-work/make_picture_vector_set.py, test/synthetic_picture_set.py and the test "make_picture_vector_set keeps one frame every two seconds" in test/meaning-search.test.mjs; the answer was produced by running the builder on two synthetic videos
start_here: Say to your AI: "Make a searchable set of what the videos in my card folder show, one frame every 2 seconds, so I can find moments by what they show."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads a folder of videos and writes four files (frames.npy, frames.jsonl, done.json, vector-set.json) into an output folder on your computer.
instructions: 1. Say which folder of videos to read and where the set goes. The AI reads this tool's row with tools:list, installs what get_it names if missing (the Workshop clone, ffmpeg, numpy, torch, open_clip_torch, pillow), and never writes in your videos folder.

2. The AI runs the command with those two folders: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/meaning-search/do-work/make_picture_vector_set.py --videos <folder of videos> --out <folder of the set>. Add --pattern "*.MP4" for some files, --every N for a frame every N seconds, --lut FILE.cube for log footage, --proxy for smaller copies. It can run for hours on a big card; run it again to go on where it stopped.
3. Read the last line it prints: {"result": {"frames", "added", "videos_done", "out"}}. Run it again on the same --out after a new card and only the new videos are added.

4. Put the vector_set member of <out>/vector-set.json, with the model it names, into a semantic-index-descriptor record of yours, then search it with tool:find-similar-to-a-vector (words become a query vector with tool:words-as-picture-vector).

worked_examples.title: Two videos become five timed frames
worked_examples.ask: Make a searchable set of what the videos in my card folder show, one frame every 2 seconds.
worked_examples.given: From tools/meaning-search/test/synthetic_picture_set.py and the builder in do-work/make_picture_vector_set.py, run on this computer with the test's stand-in picture model (a frame's mean colour) in place of CLIP, because CLIP is not installed here; frames, times and files are the same for either model. Folder card/CLIP holds red-take.mp4 (a red picture, 6 seconds) and blue-take.mp4 (a blue picture, 4 seconds), a key frame every half second. The command the AI runs after reading the row: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/meaning-search/do-work/make_picture_vector_set.py --videos card/CLIP --out set
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": {"frames": 5, "added": 5, "videos_done": 2, "out": "set"}} is the last line (out is the absolute path of the folder you gave). set/frames.jsonl then holds 5 rows: blue-take.mp4 at t 0.0 and 2.0, red-take.mp4 at t 0.0, 2.0 and 4.0, each with video, path and decoded; set/done.json is ["blue-take.mp4", "red-take.mp4"]; set/vector-set.json holds {"vector_set": {"items": {"file": "<out>/frames.jsonl"}, "vectors": {"file": "<out>/frames.npy"}, "points_to": {"file": "path", "start": "t"}}, "model": "<model that made them>", "every_seconds": 2.0, "frames": 5}.
